title: 'Money can't buy happiness': Toa Payoh hawker shares son playing chess at coffee shop, wins hearts

 singapore 'Money can't buy happiness': Toa Payoh hawker shares son playing chess at coffee shop, wins hearts
 The hawker said his son had invited a schoolmate to play chess at the coffee shop during the school holidays. PHOTO: Facebook/Poh Kee Chicken Rice PUBLISHED ON November 21, 2026 9:30 AM BY Asyiqin Nadzri A hawker's tongue-in-cheek remark about being unable to afford overseas holidays for his son has struck a chord with netizens, with many saying that simple moments with family and friends matter more than expensive trips.
 In a Facebook post on Thursday (Nov 19), Poh Kee Chicken Rice, a stall in Toa Payoh, shared a photo of the hawker's son and his friend playing chess at a coffee shop table.
 The two boys had plates of fried chicken nuggets and fries beside their chessboard.
 "When you have poor hawker parents who can't afford to bring you anywhere for the holidays.." he wrote.
 He later clarified in an edit that the boy in the photo was his son and that he was referring to his own financial circumstances, rather than passing judgement on others.
 In the comments, the stall owner also joked that his son would naturally face hardships with parents like him.
 'Simple moments matter more'
 The post drew supportive comments from netizens, many of whom felt that the boys' simple afternoon at the coffee shop was just as meaningful as an overseas holiday.
 One netizen said the photo showed that being rich was not necessarily about money, but about being "happy and enjoying" the moment.
 Others also praised the father for giving his son the opportunity to enjoy simple activities with his friend, with one netizen saying they would rather see children playing board games and sports than spending their time on their phones or iPads.
 Recalling their own childhood, a commenter said that playing at places such as the Padang, food courts and mamak shops was part of growing up, adding that the father should not see his family's circumstances as a hardship.
 One netizen summed up the sentiment by saying that "money can't buy happiness", adding that a happy, united and healthy family was worth more than material wealth.
 In an interview with Shin Min Daily News, the hawker, addressed as Fu, said his son was nine years old and had invited a schoolmate to play chess at the coffee shop during the school holidays.
 "The three of us have never travelled abroad together. Fortunately, neither my wife nor my son minded, nor did they ever ask me to travel abroad," he said.
 "But customers and friends often ask about it, which makes me feel very guilty."
 He has been running his chicken rice stall since 2005 and typically works from around 7am to 9pm, leaving him with little time to spend with his son on weekdays.
 Despite this, he said he prioritised caring for his family over keeping the stall open to earn money.
 AsiaOne has reached out to Poh Kee Chicken Rice for more information.
